questions.question: The book entitled, 'Playing it my way' has been authored by:
questions.questionHtml: The book entitled, 'Playing it my way' has been authored by:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Sachin Tendulkar.

Key Points

  • 'Playing It My Way' is the autobiography of Indian cricket legend Sachin Tendulkar.
  • The book was released on November 6, 2014, and has been written in collaboration with Boria Majumdar, a well-known cricket historian.
  • Sachin Tendulkar is considered one of the greatest batsmen in the history of cricket, often referred to as the "Little Master" or the "Master Blaster".
  • The autobiography provides a detailed account of Sachin's cricket career, personal life, and the various challenges he faced throughout his journey.

Additional Information

  • Sachin Tendulkar's Cricket Career:
    • Sachin Tendulkar debuted in international cricket at the age of 16 in 1989 against Pakistan.
    • He is the highest run-scorer of all time in international cricket, with more than 34,000 runs.
    • He holds the record for the most centuries in both Test and One-Day International (ODI) cricket.
  • Records and Achievements:
    • Sachin Tendulkar has been awarded the Bharat Ratna, India's highest civilian award, in 2014.
    • He was also honored with the Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna, Arjuna Award, and Padma Vibhushan.
  • Other Publications:
    • Besides his autobiography, books like 'Sachin: Cricketer of the Century' by Vimal Kumar and 'Sachin Tendulkar: The Man Cricket Loved Back' by ESPN Cricinfo are popular among fans.
  • Collaborator - Boria Majumdar:
    • Boria Majumdar is a distinguished cricket historian and journalist.
    • He has written several books on cricket and has been involved in various cricket-related projects.

questions.question: Who is the author of a new book titled ‘The World: A Family History’?
questions.questionHtml: Who is the author of a new book titled ‘The World: A Family History’?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Simon Sebag.

Key Points

  • Simon Sebag Montefiore is a renowned British historian and author known for his works on Russian history and biographies.
  • 'The World: A Family History' is his latest book, exploring the history of the world through the lens of family dynamics.
  • Simon Sebag Montefiore has received several accolades for his previous works, including the Costa Book Award and the Los Angeles Times Book Prize.
  • His other notable books include 'Jerusalem: The Biography', 'The Romanovs', and 'Young Stalin'.

Additional Information

  • Historical Non-Fiction:
    • Historical non-fiction books provide factual accounts of events, people, and places from the past.
    • They often involve extensive research and aim to present a truthful representation of history.
  • Biographical Works:
    • Biographies are detailed descriptions of a person's life, including their experiences, achievements, and impact on society.
    • Authors like Simon Sebag Montefiore use biographies to provide insight into historical figures and their times.
  • Family History in Historical Context:
    • Examining history through family stories offers a unique perspective on how personal relationships shape and are shaped by broader historical events.
    • This approach can make historical events more relatable and understandable for readers.
  • Accolades in Historical Writing:
    • Awards and recognitions in historical writing highlight the significance and impact of an author's contributions to the field.
    • Simon Sebag Montefiore's numerous awards underscore his prominence and expertise as a historian and author.

questions.question: Who among the following is the author of 'The God of Small Things'?

  • In the novel The God of Small Things, Arundhati Roy is aiming to
    • Portray the differences that the Indian society casts upon its people because of being born under different circumstances; the rights you are supposed to have as a human no matter, the gender or class you are from, and for the sole reason of being a human.
  • Arundhati Roy also has published several books of nonfiction including
    • The End of Imagination, Capitalism: A Ghost Story, and The Doctor and the Saint. 
  • She is also the author of The Ministry of Utmost Happiness, AZADI: Freedom. Fascism. Fiction, My Seditious Heart.

questions.question: Who among the following is the author of the book ‘The Great Indian Novel’?
questions.questionHtml: Who among the following is the author of the book ‘The Great Indian Novel’?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Shashi Tharoor.Key Points

  • The Great Indian Novel is a satirical novel by Shashi Tharoor.
  • It is first published by Viking Press in 1989.
  • It is a fictional work that takes the story of the Mahabharata, the Indian epic.
  • Figures from Indian history are transformed into characters from mythology, and the mythical story of India is retold as a history of Indian independence.
  • The work includes numerous puns and allusions to famous works about India.
  • The phrase "great Indian novel" is an allusion to the long-standing idea of the "Great American Novel".

Additional Information

  • Shashi Tharoor is an Indian former international diplomat, politician, writer and public intellectual.
  • He has been serving as a Member of Parliament for Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala, since 2009.
  • He was formerly Under-Secretary-General of the United Nations and ran for the post of Secretary-General in 2006.
  • He also serves as Chairman of the Parliamentary Standing Committee on Information Technology and All India Professionals Congress.
  • He formerly served as Chairman of the Parliamentary Standing Committee on External Affairs.

questions.question: The author of the famous novel 'Midnight's Children' is:
questions.questionHtml: The author of the famous novel 'Midnight's Children' is:
questions.solution: The author of the famous novel 'Midnight's Children' is Salman Rushdie. Salman Rushdie, a renowned British-Indian novelist, is celebrated for his Booker Prize-winning novel 'Midnight's Children' (1981), which combines magical realism with historical fiction. The novel explores India's transition from British colonialism to independence, focusing on the protagonist Saleem Sinai, born at the moment of India's independence, and his extraordinary powers.

questions.question: Who among the following wrote the book Gulamgiri?
questions.questionHtml: <font style="vertical-align: inherit;"><font style="vertical-align: inherit;">Who among the following wrote the book Gulamgiri?</font></font>

options.html: <font style="vertical-align: inherit;"><font style="vertical-align: inherit;">Swami Dayanand Saraswati</font></font>
<font style="vertical-align: inherit;"><font style="vertical-align: inherit;">Jyoti Rao Phule</font></font>
<font style="vertical-align: inherit;"><font style="vertical-align: inherit;">Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar</font></font>
<font style="vertical-align: inherit;"><font style="vertical-align: inherit;">B R Ambedkar</font></font>

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Jyoti Rao Phule.

Key Points

  • Jyoti Rao Phule was a prominent Indian social reformer and thinker.
  • He is best known for his efforts in fighting against the caste system and his work towards the upliftment of the oppressed sections of society.
  • Phule founded the Satyashodhak Samaj (Society of Seekers of Truth) in 1873 with the aim of achieving social equality.
  • His book Gulamgiri, published in 1873, is a critique of the social and economic conditions of the lower castes in India, advocating for their rights and social justice.

Additional Information

  • Swami Dayanand Saraswati
    • He was an Indian philosopher, social leader, and the founder of the Arya Samaj.
    • Dayanand Saraswati worked towards the revival of Vedic ideologies and aimed to reform Hindu society by promoting values such as education for all, gender equality, and the abolition of untouchability.
  • Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar
    • He was an Indian educator, social reformer, and writer known for his role in promoting women's education and widow remarriage in India.
    • Vidyasagar played a crucial part in modernizing Bengali prose and contributed significantly to the Bengal Renaissance.
  • B R Ambedkar
    • He was an Indian jurist, economist, and social reformer who was the principal architect of the Indian Constitution.
    • Ambedkar was a prominent leader of the Dalit community and worked tirelessly towards the eradication of social discrimination against the untouchables.
